product: Leonardo S.p.A., ticker LDO.MI on Borsa Italiana, prices in EUR. Aerospace, defence and security group: defence systems 38.9pct of FY2025 revenue, helicopters 29.8pct, aeronautical equipment 21.7pct, space 5.1pct, cybersecurity 3.5pct, other 1pct, across 131 plants (Italy 61, United States 27, United Kingdom 9).
demand: Government defence demand, strongly order driven. H1 2026 order intake was EUR16.0bn, up 45pct year on year, with backlog of EUR58.6bn, and management raised full year 2026 orders guidance. AW149 helicopters, M-346 aircraft and air defence equipment drove the increase, with higher European defence spending the stated driver.
pricing_power: Not found. No company pricing commentary was read. EBITA growth of 34pct on revenue growth of 12pct points to operating leverage and favourable mix rather than demonstrated price increases.
competition: Thales, Hensoldt, Rheinmetall, BAE Systems and Saab in European defence electronics and systems; Lockheed Martin, RTX and GE Aerospace in aerospace and rotorcraft. BNP Paribas described Leonardo as more attractive than Thales and Hensoldt, citing order growth toward the 2030 targets.
team: The board appointed Lorenzo Mariani as Chief Executive Officer and General Manager on 7 May 2026. The equity story is framed around the Michelangelo multi-domain programme and the 2030 industrial plan targets; no further executive detail was read.
market_strategy: Multi-domain integration under the Michelangelo programme and digital combat systems: SADOC 5 C5I, a digital S-band AESA radar and MBDA weapons for DDX integrated air and missile defence; GCAP in combat air; land vehicles through IDV; space and ESA work; shareholder returns via buybacks (1,001,000 shares, EUR47.23m) and dividends.
bull: H1 2026 orders +45% to EUR16.0bn, backlog EUR58.6bn, EBITA +34% on revenue +12%, FY2026 guidance raised; DDX EUR3.7bn contract signed 24 Sep 2026 with ~EUR1.7bn to Leonardo.
bear: H1 2026 free operating cash flow negative EUR249m; ~25x trailing P/E for revenue starting 2033; AlphaValue cut to Sell 7 Aug 2026; stock fell 2.26% on the DDX news.
falsifier: 9M 2026 results on 5 Nov 2026 showing free operating cash flow still negative and no further FY2026 guidance raise.
web_what_changed: H1 2026 results 29-30 Jul 2026: orders EUR16.0bn up 45pct, revenue EUR10.0bn up 12pct, EBITA EUR780m up 34pct, backlog EUR58.6bn; FY2026 orders, EBITA and cash guidance raised. Iveco Defence Vehicles consolidated from 18 Mar 2026. Buyback running since 19 May 2026. On 24 Sep 2026 the OSN joint venture signed the EUR3.7bn DDX destroyer contract. Close 24 Sep 2026 EUR49.31.
web_not_known_yesterday: On 24 Sep 2026 Orizzonte Sistemi Navali (Fincantieri 51pct, Leonardo 49pct) signed the OCCAR contract for two DDX destroyers: about EUR3.7bn including roughly EUR1.3bn of options, about EUR1.7bn to Leonardo, deliveries in 2033 and 2035. Despite this, LDO closed 24 Sep 2026 at EUR49.31, down 2.26pct, so the market treated the naval win as already priced in.
web_demand_price_volume_mix: Demand and volume led, not price. H1 2026 orders rose 45pct and backlog reached EUR58.6bn while revenue grew 12pct; EBITA grew 34pct, indicating operating leverage and product mix rather than price increases. No price or mix disclosure was found in the company material read.
web_suppliers: Key suppliers are mostly internal or joint ventures: Iveco Defence Vehicles (acquired 18 Mar 2026) for land vehicles, Fincantieri (51pct of OSN), MBDA for weapons, Elt Group for the DDX electronic warfare suite, Thales Alenia Space and Avio in space. OSN sub-supply contracts of about EUR1.8bn to Fincantieri and EUR1.7bn to Leonardo are still to be signed. No disclosed capacity constraint was found.
web_customers: National defence ministries, highly concentrated. FY2025 revenue split: Italy 23.3pct, United States 23.2pct, United Kingdom 13.1pct, rest of Europe 16.8pct. Named customers: Italian Navy and MoD (DDX), UK MoD (23 AW149, 2 Mar 2026), Romania MND (860 trucks, 10 Mar 2026), Indonesia MoD (AW149 letter of intent, 21 Jul 2026), Spain (IDV SuperAV, 17 Apr 2026), ESA (21 Sep 2026).
web_who_loses: European defence peers chasing the same budgets: Thales and Hensoldt (BNP Paribas rates Leonardo more attractive than both), Rheinmetall, BAE Systems, Saab, plus US primes in helicopters and electronic warfare. Fincantieri takes the DDX platform-integrator role and 51pct of OSN, so it captures the larger roughly EUR1.8bn share rather than Leonardo.
web_contradicting_evidence: Shares fell 2.26pct to EUR49.31 on 24 Sep 2026 despite the DDX win and sit 25.6pct below the EUR66.26 52-week high. H1 2026 free operating cash flow was still negative EUR249m. AlphaValue/Baader cut to Sell on 7 Aug 2026 after a Buy on 21 Jul 2026. Trailing P/E is about 25x on EUR1.951 TTM EPS, while DDX revenue only starts in 2033.
web_if_management_right: The FY2026 upgrades to orders, EBITA and free cash flow are met, the EUR58.6bn backlog converts, and rising European defence budgets, which BNP cites as moving toward 3pct of GDP, fund drones, cyber, land systems and GCAP. The 2030 plan targets are achieved; the consensus mean target of EUR69.41 implies roughly 40pct upside from EUR49.31.
web_if_management_wrong: Execution and cash break first: negative H1 2026 free operating cash flow, Iveco Defence Vehicles integration and working capital. Second is the valuation multiple, about 25x trailing earnings for growth that lands in 2033-2035 programmes. A European budget slippage or DDX delay would trigger downgrades of the AlphaValue Sell type.
web_second_order_beneficiaries: Fincantieri (51pct of OSN and platform integrator), MBDA (missiles), Elt Group (DDX electronic warfare suite), Avio and Thales Alenia Space (space), IDV and Indra Land Vehicles (Spain VACIM), the Italian SME supply chain, AESA radar and electronics subcontractors, and training and simulation providers.
